title: Canadian intern and suspected NATO spy to await trial under electronic monitoring
summary: Biwei Zhang, the 33-year-old computer scientist accused of spying on NATO, will be under electronic monitoring while awaiting trial, a Belgian court ruled on Wednesday.
byline: Aloysius Wong, Idil Mussa, Albert Leung

image.caption: 33-year-old computer scientist Biwei Zhang will continue her pretrial detention under electronic monitoring, a Belgian court decided today. Zhang was arrested in July amid allegations of spying on NATO's military headquarters, where she was working as an intern. (Reuters, Catina Zhang/Facebook)

blocks.text: Biwei Zhang, the 33-year-old computer scientist accused of spying on NATO, will be under electronic monitoring while awaiting trial, a Belgian court ruled on Wednesday.
Belgian federal prosecutor's office considering launching appeal
· Posted: Nov 25, 2026 1:30 PM EST | Last Updated: 30 minutes ago
The Canadian intern accused of spying on NATO on behalf of China will continue her pretrial detention under electronic monitoring, a Belgian court decided Wednesday.
Belgian prosecutors are considering lodging an appeal against the decision, the federal prosecutor's office said in a press release.
The prosecutors did not immediately clarify whether there were other conditions placed on the suspect.

Biwei Zhang, 33, was an intern at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) when she was arrested in July and charged with "spying on behalf of a third country and of being a member of a criminal organization."

Zhang — who is also known by the names Claire and Catina — has a background in computer science and economics and previously worked for Canadian federal agencies including StatsCan and the Canadian Space Agency.
The allegations against Zhang have not been tested in court.
Neither Zhang nor her lawyer have responded to past CBC News requests for comment.
